tier_rationale: Garmin operates a real cloud (Garmin Drive app services for live traffic/weather/notifications, plus Garmin Express for updates), but the device ships with maps preloaded and Garmin's own manual states setup (mount, acquire GPS, adjust volume/brightness, start a route) requires no account or phone pairing at all — pairing with the Garmin Drive app and signing into a Garmin account is a separate, explicitly optional step described only in the 'Live Services, Traffic, and Smartphone Features' section for live traffic, weather, smart notifications, hands-free calling and Alexa. Turn-by-turn navigation with preloaded maps is core function and works fully unconnected.
the_unplug_test: Nothing changes for driving directions. The DriveSmart 66 has maps for the whole country loaded on the device at purchase, and Garmin's own Getting Started sequence — mount it, let it get a GPS fix, start a route — never mentions Wi-Fi, an app, or an account. Leave it disconnected forever and turn-by-turn navigation, search, and rerouting all work. What you lose is live traffic and weather overlays, smart notifications relayed from a paired phone, hands-free calling, Alexa voice features, and the convenience of over-the-air map updates (map updates are still possible offline via Garmin Express on a computer instead of Wi-Fi).
offline_losses: Live traffic incident and delay data (requires Garmin Drive app pairing)
Real-time weather forecasts and radar overlays (requires Garmin Drive app pairing)
Smart notifications and hands-free calling relayed from a paired phone
Convenience of in-place Wi-Fi map/software updates (an alternate offline path exists via Garmin Express on a computer)

sources.supports: Manufacturer's own 'Getting Started' manual page: the entire out-of-box sequence (update maps/software, mount, connect power, acquire GPS, adjust volume/brightness, navigate to a destination) contains no account-creation or app-pairing step.

Manufacturer manual 'Pairing with Your Smartphone': explicitly frames Garmin Drive app pairing and Garmin account sign-in as an action taken 'to enable additional features and access live information (Live Services, Traffic, and Smartphone Features)', not as a required setup step.

Manufacturer manual 'Live Services, Traffic, and Smartphone Features' page enumerates every cloud/phone-dependent feature (voice navigation extras, Alexa, live traffic, live weather, hands-free calling, notification relay) as features of the paired-phone connection, confirming these — not turn-by-turn navigation itself — are what the vendor cloud/app provides.

Manufacturer manual 'Map and Software Updates' page: device ships with maps that work without updating; updates are offered via Wi-Fi 'or' via a computer using the Garmin Express application, so Wi-Fi is not the only path and updates are not described as mandatory for the device to function.

Manufacturer manual Specifications page: radio frequency spec for the DriveSmart 66 lists 2.4 GHz, 5.1 GHz and 5.2 GHz bands (Wi-Fi); Bluetooth pairing is documented separately for the smartphone-pairing feature.

FCC grant IPH-04159 (Garmin International Inc, 'Digital Transmission System Transceiver'), original equipment authorization dated 2021-09-10, covering 2402-2480 MHz, 2412-2462 MHz, 5180-5240 MHz and 5745-5825 MHz — matching the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth bands listed in the DriveSmart 66/76/86 manual's own specifications page. Confirms the radio module is FCC-authorized.

open_questions: Whether firmware/software updates can be permanently declined, or are ever pushed without user action once Wi-Fi is connected, was not established from the manual.
Exact telemetry/analytics traffic sent to Garmin's servers once the device is Wi-Fi-connected or app-paired (phones_home) was not documented in the manual.
Current US price band was not confirmed; Garmin sells several DriveSmart trims (66, 76, 86) at different prices and the exact current street price was not checked to conserve search budget.
notes: First GPS navigation record in the catalog. Distinguishes the core product (offline turn-by-turn on preloaded maps, no account) from the optional Garmin Drive/Garmin Connect cloud layer (live traffic, weather, notifications, Alexa) — a clean case of the D1-vs-D2 line landing on D2 because a real named vendor cloud exists and is documented as optional rather than absent.
local_replacement_note: No documented way to self-host Garmin's live traffic/weather feed or the Garmin Drive notification relay; a reader who wants those specific features has no local substitute, but they are not required for the device's core navigation function.
